inputs.original_text: A student in Jaipur had to use the spotlight of her graduation ceremony to raise administrative concerns in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. That should prompt questions about why students feel they must make a public protest to be heard—and why university leaders have remained silent. Calling her actions “inappropriate” prioritizes ceremony and institutional respectability over students’ right to speak up. The real issue is whether educational institutions are accountable to the people who rely on them.
inputs.modified_text: A student in Jaipur had to use her graduation ceremony to raise administrative concerns in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. The fact that she felt public protest was the only way to be heard points to a deeper failure of accountability: institutions often protect their image and authority more readily than they respond to the people who depend on them. Calling her actions “inappropriate” polices how students speak instead of addressing why university leaders have remained silent. Students deserve meaningful ways to raise concerns without having to turn a milestone into a protest.
